claim: `run` reads `head` before `keep_alive`, which commits and pushes a `saved` event when the ticket's last event is at least `save_minutes` old; after the reviewer, `git reset --hard head` moves the branch back behind that pushed commit. The review run is then committed on the old head and its push is refused as a non-fast-forward, so the run never reaches the remote and every later push of the branch is refused too (sequence: a ticket in `reviewing`, `rail advance` more than ten minutes after its last event, such as a session coming back from a pause or after an invalid-output review).
check: A test that runs `rail advance` on a ticket in `reviewing` whose last event is older than `[claim] save_minutes`, and asserts that the local branch and the remote branch have the same tip afterwards.

claim: With this engine ticket 8 is no longer `merged`: its contract pull request #11 was merged with no ship, so it becomes `new` with owner `agent` (CONTRACT_MERGED). After ticket 9 merges, the next `rail next` records the merge as the owner's approval of ticket 8 and hands an agent the same contract ticket 9 just delivered; nothing in the change drops ticket 8 or says a person must.
check: After the change, `rail status --json` lists no ticket with owner `agent` whose Done Contract equals that of a merged ticket; here, ticket 8 is dropped before or with the merge.

reason: The sign of life is now written before the review run reads the head it resets the worktree to (review.py); a test with save_minutes = 0 checks the branch stays in step with the remote across two reviews.

Ticket 8 is dropped: a dropped event on its branch and a 'rail drop 8' mark on the counter branch rail/ids. The engine now marks every drop there, so a dropped ticket whose contract reached the base stays dropped when its branch is deleted (state.py, project.py), with a test.

claim: A `cd` the guard can't follow is recognised only when `cd`, `pushd` or `popd` is the first word of a simple command. After `cd OTHER_REPO &&`, a `cd -` inside a brace group, after `then`, or after `!` is missed, so the push to `main` or `gh pr merge` that follows is judged as the other repository's and allowed. This is the sweep's F1 case in another spelling, and `docs/guards.md` says whatever can't be followed is judged as this project's.
check: A guard test that expects deny for `cd OTHER && { cd -; git push origin main; }`, `cd OTHER && if true; then cd -; fi && git push origin main` and `cd OTHER && ! cd - && git push origin main`, where OTHER is another git repository.

claim: The ticket's Why says work a session abandoned is resumed after an hour, but the engine copied in resumes it after `[claim] stale_minutes` = 30 (config.py default, and the ticket's own Look at says 30 minutes). The Why becomes the pull request's description, so the owner is told twice the real limit.

reason: The guard now strips shell keywords ({, !, if, then, elif, else, do, while, until) before reading a command, so a cd or a push behind one is seen; tests cover the four spellings reported and plain keyword commands that must still pass.
The ticket's Why now says 30 minutes with no sign of life, as the engine does.

claim: `_save_note` reads the cache with key `session or ""`, so with no `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` it opens the directory `rail/cache/hooks/` and `rail next` dies with a traceback. Sequence: any Claude session has started in the clone (the SessionStart hook creates that folder), then `rail next --ticket 1` or a bare `rail next` runs from a plain terminal or another agent; the claim is committed before the crash.
check: A test that runs the session-start hook with a session id, then `rail next --ticket NN` with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID unset, and expects exit 0 with an IMPLEMENT brief.

claim: The save hooks don't know a review is running: when the session's PostToolUse hook fires while its own `rail advance` is inside a review (a parallel tool call, or advance run in the background), `save_work` commits and pushes the reviewer's in-scope scratch files. The review's `git reset --hard head` then moves the branch back behind that push, so the `review` commit never reaches the remote and local and remote stay diverged (the same end state as F1).
check: A test whose review command writes a file inside scope_paths and sleeps, runs `rail hook pulse` for the same session meanwhile, and asserts the remote branch has no scratch file and equals the local branch after advance.

reason: cache_read returns nothing for an empty key or a folder, and the save note is only read when the session has an id. Test: test_next_works_from_a_plain_terminal_after_a_claude_session in the framework's tests/test_save.py (framework commit 9104f6c).

An engine command that works in a ticket's worktree (advance, a transition from next, sweep) now holds a per-ticket file lock, and a save skips a ticket that is held. Test: test_a_save_stays_out_while_advance_is_inside_a_review (framework commit 9104f6c); it fails without the hold.

claim: `_known` expands `$OLDPWD` with the hook process's own environment, not the shell's value at that point in the command. So `cd OTHER_REPO && cd "$OLDPWD" && git push origin main` (the same as `cd -`, sweep F1) is allowed whenever the hook inherits an OLDPWD outside the project, although docs/guards.md says a variable the guard can't follow is judged as this project's.
check: A guard test that sets OLDPWD in the hook's environment to a directory outside the project and expects deny for `cd OTHER && cd "$OLDPWD" && git push origin main`; variables the shell changes during a command (OLDPWD, PWD) should count as unknown.

reason: The guard no longer expands variables from the hook's environment: it follows only ~, $HOME and $PWD (the place it followed the command to); any other variable, $OLDPWD included, is judged as this project's. Test: test_a_variable_is_not_read_from_the_hooks_own_environment in the framework's tests/test_guards.py (framework commit 1da6ab9); it fails on the old guard with the reviewer's command.

claim: A `cd` is recognised only as the first word after wrappers and keywords, and `builtin` and `eval` are neither. So after `cd OTHER_REPO &&`, `builtin cd - && git push origin main` (or `eval cd - && ...`, or `gh pr merge 5` in place of the push) is still judged as the other repository's and allowed, although the shell is back in this project; this is F3's case in one more spelling.
check: A guard test that `cd OTHER && builtin cd - && git push origin main` and the same with `eval cd -` are denied, next to the existing keyword-spelling tests.

reason: The guard now reads the command that runs: builtin and other wrappers with their own options and arguments are unwrapped (builtin cd -, timeout 60 git push -f, xargs, sudo -u NAME, /usr/bin/git), and the commands of bash -c and eval are judged too. After a sourced file, an eval it can't read, or env -C DIR, a command is judged as this project's. Tests: test_a_command_inside_a_wrapper_or_a_shell_is_still_that_command and the added cases in test_a_cd_the_guard_cannot_follow_leaves_the_rules_in_force (framework commit bcb7d37); both fail on the old guard.

claim: `save_work` passes every dirty path to `git add -A -- <paths>`, which dies with `pathspec did not match any files` for a staged deletion. After `git rm src/old.py` in a ticket's worktree (or one save after `git mv`, which commits only the new name and leaves `D old` staged), every `rail save` exits 2 and the Stop and pulse hooks fail without telling the agent: nothing is pushed and no `saved` event is written, so the work isn't saved and the ticket looks abandoned to other sessions after 30 minutes.
check: A test in tests/test_save.py: claim a ticket, `git rm` (and separately `git mv`) an in-scope file in its worktree, run `rail save` twice, and assert exit 0, a `saved` event, and the deletion on the remote branch.

reason: A save now stages only paths that are still on disk or in the index, so a staged deletion no longer stops git add, and a rename counts as both of its names, so the old name's deletion is committed with the new one. A save that fails in the pulse hook is told to the agent. Tests: test_a_save_takes_deleted_and_renamed_files and test_a_save_that_fails_in_a_hook_is_told_to_the_agent (framework commit 2ebe661); both fail on the old code.

claim: A ticket file on the base branch with no branch and no ship is now recorded as `accepted by person via merge`, with no check that a person merged a contract pull request. Ticket files are excluded from the scope check, so an auto-merged LOW ticket whose branch adds `.rail/tickets/99.md` (tier HIGH, scope `.rail/engine/**`) gets the HIGH contract approved and claimed by the next `rail next` with no person involved; the engine on main showed the same ticket as `dropped`.
check: A test: commit a HIGH ticket file to the base branch under another ticket's `Ticket:` trailer, with no branch and no pull request, run `rail next`, and assert no `accepted` event with `by: person` is written.

claim: `_gh_named` treats any `gh` argument containing `github.com/` as naming a repository, including the value of `--body` or `-f`, so a merge of this project's pull request passes when its message mentions another repository's URL: `gh pr merge 5 --body "see github.com/other/repo"`. The engine on main denied this command; with the new rule that a merged unshipped pull request counts as the person's approval, it also lets an agent approve its own contract.
check: A guard test: `gh pr merge 5 --body "see github.com/other/repo"` and `gh api -X PUT repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/5/merge -f commit_message=https://github.com/other/repo/issues/1` must both return deny.

claim: The new Stop and PostToolUse hooks commit and push every untracked file inside `scope_paths` with no check, and `.gitignore` lists only `.claude/worktrees/` and `__pycache__/`. A credential or dump file an agent writes into an in-scope folder (for example `calc/token.json` under scope `calc/**`) is pushed to GitHub at the end of the turn, before verify's secret scan ever runs.
check: A test that `save_work` leaves out untracked files matching the guard's secret patterns (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`), or runs the project's secret scan before the push.

claim: The merge deny matches only `gh pr merge` with the two words adjacent, and the guard doesn't read command substitutions or `case` arms, so `gh pr -R timur-makarov/throw-away-repo merge 5`, `echo $(git push origin HEAD:main)` in backticks or `$(...)`, `case x in x) git push -f origin x;; esac` and `cd /tmp && export GIT_DIR=<repo>/.git && git push origin main` all pass. These passed on main's engine too.
check: Guard tests for each of these lines expecting deny.
